items.title: Claude Code can edit your videos now
items.summary: Claude Code can edit your videos now. Here is the whole setup, step by step, on your own computer. Make a folder, unzip the kit inside it, and open Claude Code in that folder so it can read everything. Install ffmpeg and Python, both free, and run the install script with the whisper option so it downloads the speech model. Talk to Claude while you record. Whisper writes your spoken notes into the transcript, so Claude reads them. Then drop the clip in the folder and run the podcast-to-clips command. It picks the moment, cuts it and adds captions. Cut check re-listens and flags any word it swallowed. The kit has the 17 effects I built from one take of me, plus the editing skills. Idea: @millee.md #shorts #claudecode #videoediting

items.title: The Right Model for Each Coding Task
items.summary: Weave (YC W25) helps engineering teams understand whether their AI coding tools are actually making them more productive. Its models measure the work humans and agents produce and compare that output with AI spending. The company recently raised a $13.5M Series A led by Standard Capital and launched Weave Router, which selects models for different coding tasks. In this Fireside, co-founders Adam Cohen and Andrew Churchill discuss how they went from measuring human productivity to optimizing coding agents, why cost per output matters more than raw token spend, and how their AI coach helps engineers work more effectively with agents. They also share their vision for autonomous software factories and explain why combining different models’ strengths could outperform any single model. https://weaveos.com Chapters: 00:00 — Optimizing AI Coding With Weave 04:02 — Getting More From Your AI Budget 08:39 — Measuring Work Beyond Lines of Code 12:30 — From AI Adoption to Optimization 16:47 — Measuring AI ROI and Coaching Engineers 20:16 — Building Software Factories 25:38 — The Future of Model Routing Apply to Y Combinator: https://www.ycombinator.com/apply Work at a startup: https://www.ycom...

items.summary: How did the race to build AGI really unfold, and who made the decisions that shaped it? Tech journalist Kevin Roose interviewed 150 people at the center of the AI industry to find out. items.title: 10 Habits PhDs Must Unlearn To Build a Startup | Startup School
items.summary: Google, Anthropic, and Databricks were all started by founders with PhDs. But they’re the exceptions. Most academic founders fail, because the instincts that get you published are the ones that can get you killed in a startup. Francois Chaubard knows both sides. He’s a visiting partner at YC and a current PhD student, and before that he was a researcher in Fei-Fei Li’s lab and the founder and CEO of Focal. In this episode of Startup School, Francois breaks down the ten mindset shifts you have to make to go from researcher to formidable founder. He'll cover how to thrive without deadlines or grades, the difference between an interesting idea and an important one, and why being the first to an idea can actually be a disadvantage. items.title: datasette-agent 0.5a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-agent 0.5a0 This is a significant release of Datasette Agent . The most notable new feature is called the panel - it lets the agent chat open and then sit next to pages from Datasette, for example a table or query page. When combined with datasette-apps this means you can prompt a database-backed app into existence and then modify it from the chat that sits next to that app. You can try it by signing in with your GitHub account to agent.datasette.io .
